title: Raiders, tight end Michael Mayer agree to contract extension
content:
HENDERSON, Nev. — The Las Vegas Raiders and tight end Michael Mayer have agreed to a multi-year contract extension, the team announced Saturday. It’s a three-year deal worth $45 million with $30 million in guarantees, per a league source who was not permitted to speak on a deal that was not yet finalized.

Mayer’s new $15 million average salary makes him the NFL’s fifth-highest-paid tight end, in terms of average annual value. Only George Kittle, Trey McBride, Kyle Pitts and the newly-inked Tucker Kraft sit ahead of him. Mayer’s deal is the largest three-year extension for a tight end in NFL history.

Mayer, a 2023 second-round pick out of Notre Dame, is entering his fourth year in Las Vegas and is set for a bigger role in new coach Klint Kubiak’s heavy-set scheme. That role will expand even more with star Brock Bowers out to start the season due to knee surgery.

The 25-year-old Mayer has 788 receiving yards on 83 catches for three touchdowns in his career. He’s coming off his best season, in which he had 35 catches for 328 yards and a touchdown. Since the Raiders drafted Bowers in 2024, Mayer has served in a complementary role. Still, with Kubiak utilizing multiple tight ends in his offense, he’ll become more of a receiving threat, even when Bowers returns.

“I really love this offense, I really love Klint,” Mayer said during training camp. “It’s just about being comfortable, being the type of player that I can be, and going out there and showing people.”

For now, Mayer will be the focal point at the tight end position without Bowers. The extension proves that the Raiders are confident he can excel in the role.

“Mike does a lot of things well, and we try to emphasize what he does well in the run game, what he does well in the pass game,” offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko said this week. “Just the way he finishes each play with the ball in his hand. I think that’s something that gives us an advantage.”

Not only is Mayer the first member of the Raiders’ 2023 draft class to receive an extension, but he is also just one of three players from the class remaining on the team, along with wide receiver Tre Tucker and quarterback Aidan O’Connell.
